A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same DCCD research despite the changed title. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across versions.

before.justification: v1 reports original structured-generation experiments on GSM8K, GSM-Symbolic, MATH500, and FOLIO, plus scaling, confidence, and summarization results.

after.justification: v2 retains those empirical results and adds controlled comparisons, latency measurements, draft analyses, schema-tightness tests, and a reasoning-model comparison.

M1.justification: The two-stage draft-then-constrain procedure, masking equations, and Algorithm 1 remain substantively unchanged. Multiple drafts, feasible-mass selection, and alternative selection rules were already described in v1; v2 adds evaluations of these choices.

E1.justification: Appendix L.5 adds a stricter GSM8K output scenario requiring an integer answer instead of the existing string-valued answer. This narrowly expands tested output requirements; the datasets, domains, and summarization coverage otherwise remain unchanged.

E2.justification: The original CP/CF/CD comparison in Table 2 is retained. Additional comparisons introduce unconstrained generation alongside DCCD, thinking-style generation with CD restricted to the answer stage using DeepSeek R1 Qwen 1.5B, and a direct feasible-mass-versus-majority-voting comparison (Tables 5, 6, 11, and 13). These substantially broaden the evaluated alternatives.

E3.justification: v2 adds answer-correctness evaluation separating prompt wording from masking, equal total generation budgets of 600 or 900 tokens, draft caps from 256 to 2048 tokens, and K=5 selection comparisons. It also introduces batched latency/adherence measurements and a reasoning-model configuration. These are substantial additional evaluation protocols.

E4.justification: Section 5.3 and Appendix L add controls and ablations addressing prompt versus masking effects, token-budget confounding, draft length, draft-error propagation, feasible mass versus correctness, selection rules, and schema tightness. Additional few-shot success/failure examples supplement the retained case studies.

E5.justification: Appendix L.3 newly reports a Pearson correlation of 0.71 between cumulative log feasible mass and final correctness and calls it statistically significant. This adds statistical reporting, although no significance test, p-value, confidence interval, or repeated-run information is supplied.

E6.justification: Table 2 and the original scaling and summarization results are unchanged, but Tables 3 and 5–13 add substantial results. For example, the new 900-token 1B comparison reports 6.40% for CD versus 15.80% for DCCD, and Table 13 reports 51.2% for thinking plus answer-stage CD versus 62.6% for DCCD. These are additional comparisons, not revisions to the original benchmark scores.

T1.justification: The feasible-mass definitions, reverse-KL projection argument, sequence reweighting identity, and Appendix A utility bound using Pinsker's inequality are retained. Equation renumbering and the new illustrative KL-drift figure do not introduce a new derivation or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about training-free DCCD, projection-tax reduction, structured accuracy, parameter efficiency, and test-time scaling. The new title changes emphasis, while the added experiments support existing contributions.

C2.justification: v2 explicitly discusses additional latency, dependence on draft quality, limited correction of incorrect drafts, and feasible mass as a distortion proxy rather than a correctness measure. It also interprets the new controls as separating masking effects from prompt effects and showing benefits beyond additional token budget (Section 5.3 and Appendix L).

D1.justification: v2 specifies batched vLLM execution on a single NVIDIA H100 for timing, token-budget splits and draft caps for new analyses, and the R1 drafter/Qwen projector pairing. Existing prompts, grammars, schemas, and the code-access link are retained; reproducibility documentation is extended rather than comprehensively revised.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations to Xiao et al. (2016) and Yin and Neubig (2017), and Appendix L.6 discusses DCCD's relationship to thinking-token generation. The main related-work discussion and positioning against existing constrained-decoding approaches remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: The title and publication header change, with localized wording edits, a clarification about few-shot examples, and additional analysis subsections. Most existing prose and the main section structure are retained; the expansion primarily consists of new scientific content.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands the visual presentation with a full-width method diagram, prompt-decomposition and diagnostic tables, a two-panel KL-drift illustration, and additional boxed examples. Existing performance plots are mostly relocated or renumbered. Several new example boxes are duplicated between Appendices G and J.4.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked equal-token controls and supported efficiency mainly through parameter counts. v2 adds those controls, measured runtime/adherence tradeoffs, prompt-versus-masking comparisons, and draft-error diagnostics, substantially strengthening evaluation of the central proposal. Reporting issues temper these gains: Table 12 gives a 3B GSM8K baseline of 81.58 versus 73.24 in Table 2, and correlation significance lacks a specified test. These limit individual analyses, but the new controls and explicit failure conditions provide a substantial net improvement.
